scores.evidence: Phase 1: Foundation & Toolchain ... Phase 4: Observability & Reliability
scores.rationale: Broadly substrate-upward, but nothing is proven before dependents, and observability and GitOps come after deployment automation.
There is no thin end-to-end production slice early. Phase 1 is infrastructure only, and pilot services do not arrive until Phase 5.
Choices are listed as open options with no defaults or flip conditions, so irreversible decisions are not gated.
Onboarding is staged by batch, but the ordering starts with the least complex services rather than the widest-impact work.

scores.evidence: Implement secrets vault (HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager)
scores.rationale: Security appears in Phase 1 (secrets, RBAC) and in Phase 2 (SAST). It is absent from the later phases, and hardening is left to the end.
Basic logging and monitoring are in Phase 1, but the main observability work is in Phase 4, and later phases do not treat it concretely.
Versioning, config as code and GitOps appear, but GitOps comes late and reproducibility is not threaded through every phase.
Rollback appears in Phases 2 and 3, but DR and chaos engineering are left to the end.
The plan never says whether an AI layer applies, so it does not declare N/A.
Later work is grouped into a phase, but there are no explicit deferrals and no pull-forward conditions.

note: This is a generic phased checklist. It has no walking skeleton, no decision gates and no deferral triggers, and observability, security and resilience are mostly late or partial.
